text: By the end of this decade, Kestrelline Rail will site its new maintenance depot on the reclaimed eastern yards of Port Ansgar, according to plans confirmed Tuesday by the company’s board. The facility, expected to open in late 2029, will replace the aging works at Brackhollow and concentrate heavy repairs, cleaning bays and wheel lathe operations under one roof. Kestrelline says the £184 million project will support 260 jobs, with another 90 apprenticeships to follow over five years. For Port Ansgar, long shaped by salt wind and shipping cranes, the choice carries a certain historical symmetry: the city once sent out rail steel, and now, at last, it will host the trains themselves when they return for upkeep.
